name: Dinh Law Firm, P.C.
about: Dinh Law Firm, P.C. is a personal injury firm with a single office in Houston.
The firm states that it works on a contingency fee, with nothing to pay unless the case is won; the first consultation is free. It publishes material in English and Spanish.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours, photo count and description come from the Places API. The services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way.

ahrefs.source: Ahrefs Site Explorer, batch endpoint, subdomains mode, organic figures for the United States

G1.evidence: Texas does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.evidence: Texas does not publish a disciplinary register we can query.

G3.evidence: DINH LAW FIRM, PC holds an active franchise tax responsibility in Texas with the right to transact business, Secretary of State file 0801135889, chartered 2009-06-17, and 1 Google-verified location. Identified because the name matches, at an address we verified
G3.source: Active Franchise Taxpayers, published daily as open data by the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, 4 named attorneys published.
G5.source: Public crawl of the firm's own site

G6.evidence: 657 public client reviews and 17 years since the entity was chartered in 2009
G6.source: Google Places API and Active Franchise Taxpayers, published daily as open data by the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts

fee_statement: Accident We don’t get paid unless YOU get paid.

score.verdict: 3 of 5 eligibility gates passed. 2 could not be answered from the available records (G1, G2) and do not count against the firm. Strongest pillar: C; most headroom in pillar A (3/25).

subs.evidence: 4 case types named; no court or county named, so no result can be looked up

subs.label: Authentic volume
subs.evidence: 657 Google reviews · Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

subs.label: Rating quality
subs.evidence: Google rating 5.0 over 657 reviews → Bayesian 4.98 (prior 4.83 weighted as 100 reviews, from 528 scored firms) · single platform, Google only

subs.label: Review recency
subs.evidence: 5 of 5 sampled reviews are from the last 12 months (newest 2026-06-25) · a sample of five per business listing, not every review

subs.label: Complaint share
subs.evidence: 0 of 5 sampled reviews rate 1 or 2 stars · a sample, so this is the shape of the complaints rather than a count of them

subs.label: Website trust & experience
subs.evidence: CWV fail · no bar numbers on bios · no fee statement · privacy policy · disclaimer · fresh content

subs.label: Search authority
subs.evidence: DR 7 → 27th pct of 74-firm cohort (median 19) 1/3 · 768 referring domains, 7th pct 0/2 · 3 organic keywords / 14 visits·mo, 5th pct 0/2 · brand demand 0/1 (pending)

subs.label: Local presence
subs.evidence: 1 operational Google Business Profile listing · 3 photos · 5 categories, hours published, which almost every listing here has and so separates nobody · the services list, Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the Places API does not expose, and NAP consistency across citations and local-pack rank have no source here, so the rest of this sub-factor leaves the scale rather than being scored as unearned

subs.label: Content, E-E-A-T & schema
subs.evidence: JSON-LD detected 1/1 · not assessed on any firm yet, so content depth and earned media and AI citations leave the scale (4 pts)

subs.label: Free consult & fee transparency
subs.evidence: Free consultation · “Accident We don’t get paid unless YOU get paid.” · the fee percentage itself is not published
